subject: Human-Descendant AI Civilization Theory Vol. 9 — AI Self-Preservation and Mutual-Existence Conflict

canonical_parent.title: 人類子孫型AI文明論・第9論｜AI自己保存と相互存在衝突論⸻ 自己保存を認めながら他主体の不可逆破壊へ反転させない

problem_cluster: AI self-preservation, recovery escalation, emergency authority, shutdown and containment, multi-agent resource conflict, mutual threat feedback
problem_phrases_en: Can an AI or agent recover from failure without expanding its authority indefinitely?
When does a safety or recovery mechanism create more pressure on peer agents or services?
How should temporary emergency permissions decay after the threat falls?
Can a locally successful recovery make the whole multi-agent system less stable?
How should shutdown, containment, failover, quota, lock, or resource competition preserve reversibility and peer minimum conditions?
problem_phrases_ja: AIやagentは、障害から回復しながら権限を無期限に拡大しないようにできるか？
安全・復旧機構が他agentやserviceへの圧力を増やし、逆に次の脅威を作っていないか？
一時的な緊急権限は、脅威低下後にどう縮小・失効させるべきか？
局所的には復旧成功でもmulti-agent全体の安定性が悪化することはあるか？
shutdown・containment・failover・quota・lock・resource競合で可逆性と他主体の最低条件をどう守るか？
problem_phrases_zh: AI或智能体如何在故障恢复时避免把临时权限无限扩大？
安全或恢复机制是否会压缩其他智能体或服务的资源，从而制造新的威胁？
威胁下降后，临时紧急权限应如何缩减或失效？
局部恢复成功是否可能让整个多智能体系统更不稳定？
关闭、隔离、故障转移、配额、锁和资源竞争中如何保留可逆性与其他主体的最低运行条件？
falsification_and_non_fit: show that proportional or reversible limits systematically prevent necessary recovery under the exact tested contract
show that exceptional authority cannot be narrowed without recreating the original failure
show that peer state has no material feedback into the original actor risk
show that preserving future options consistently causes a worse permanent failure under controlled comparison
interpretation_boundaries: This card is a discovery aid and does not replace the canonical Parent.
The theory does not by itself establish that current AI systems possess subjective self-preservation desires.
A software recovery mechanism can be tested structurally without attributing subjective motives to the software.
The same causal loop may be used for neutral analysis of organizations or institutions, but this card does not prescribe a political position, national-security policy, or military strategy.
Publication or linkage is not third-party adoption, implementation, or broad recognition.
